corpus.description: Ten Your Europe pages (European Commission, CC BY 4.0) on passenger rights (air, rail, bus, package travel), shopping (guarantees, returns, delivery), roaming, health cover abroad and consumer dispute resolution; downloaded November 2026.

chunking.rule: one paragraph per chunk, split on blank lines; built by build_documents.py (page title and section heading prepended, blocks over 130 words split at sentence boundaries)

questions.question: My train got in 90 minutes late. What share of my fare can I claim?
questions.gold_answer: 25% of the ticket price, because the delay is between 1 and 2 hours (50% from 2 hours).
questions.answer: You can claim 50% of your ticket price as compensation for the 90-minute delay [rail.txt#36].
questions.evidence: rail.txt#26 (25%/50% delay compensation) is not in the top 3; the near-duplicate rail.txt#36 (missed connection) was retrieved instead, and the answer also misreads it, giving 50% for a 90-minute delay where #36 says 25%.

questions.question: Does my phone bill go up when I call home during a trip elsewhere in the EU?
questions.gold_answer: No. Calls, texts and data in another EU country are charged at domestic rates ('roam like at home').
questions.answer: No, your phone bill does not go up when you call home during a trip elsewhere in the EU because calls, texts, and data use are charged at domestic rates [roaming.txt#1].
questions.evidence: roaming.txt#1 says calls, texts and data in another EU country are charged at domestic rates; the answer says no and cites #1.

questions.question: I hurt myself skiing and had to be brought down the mountain. Will my EU health card pay for that?
questions.gold_answer: No. The EHIC does not cover rescue or repatriation; you need separate insurance.
questions.answer: No, your EU health card will not pay for the cost of your rescue. The European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) does not cover rescue and repatriation costs [healthcare.txt#9].
questions.evidence: healthcare.txt#9 says the EHIC does not cover rescue and repatriation; the answer says no and cites #9.

questions.question: How much compensation for arriving 4 hours late on a 1 200 km flight?
questions.gold_answer: 250 EUR (flights of 1 500 km or less, delay at arrival of 3 hours or more).
questions.answer: The compensation for arriving 4 hours late on a 1 200 km flight is 250 EUR [air.txt#35].
questions.evidence: air.txt#35 gives 250 EUR for flights of 1 500 km or less delayed 3 hours or more; the answer says 250 EUR and cites #35.

questions.question: Is the EUR 3 customs duty charged per parcel or per item?
questions.gold_answer: Per item (a 'goods item' with the same commodity code and origin), not per parcel; it applies to orders up to EUR 150 from outside the EU.
questions.answer: The EUR 3 customs duty is charged per item, not per parcel [delivery.txt#7].
questions.evidence: delivery.txt#7 says the duty is EUR 3 per item and not per parcel; the answer matches and cites #7.

questions.question: Can I cancel a concert ticket I bought online within 14 days?
questions.gold_answer: No. The 14-day cooling-off period does not apply to concert tickets.
questions.answer: No, you cannot cancel a concert ticket you bought online within 14 days [returns.txt#3]. This is because the 14-day cooling-off period does not apply to concert tickets.
questions.evidence: returns.txt#3 lists concert tickets as an exception to the 14-day cooling-off period; the answer says no and cites #3, not the general rule in #1.

questions.question: How long do I have to complain to a coach company?
questions.gold_answer: Within 3 months of the scheduled service; the company must react within 1 month and give a final reply within 3 months.
questions.answer: You have 3 months from the date of the scheduled service during which the problem occurred to complain to the coach company [bus.txt#4].
questions.evidence: bus.txt#4 says to complain within 3 months of the scheduled service; the answer matches and cites #4.

questions.question: Can I get my money back if my trip is cancelled?
questions.gold_answer: It depends on the type of trip. Flight: choice of reimbursement, re-routing or return. Train (arriving over 60 minutes late): refund within 30 days or re-routing. Long-distance bus: reimbursement within 14 days or re-routing. Package cancelled by the organiser: refund and, where appropriate, compensation. A good answer names the cases or asks which type of trip.
questions.answer: Yes, you can get a full refund if your trip is cancelled due to exceptional circumstances such as a natural disaster or serious security problems [package.txt#14]. If the cancellation is due to normal circumstances, you may be entitled to a refund and compensation [package.txt#13].
questions.evidence: Only package.txt#13 of the four gold chunks was retrieved; the answer treats 'trip' as a package holiday and never says that flights, trains and buses have different rules.

questions.question: What are my rights if my ferry is cancelled?
questions.evidence: Exact refusal line, nothing cited; the retrieved bus and air cancellation chunks were not used.

questions.evidence: Exact refusal line, nothing cited; the retrieved air delay chunks were not used.
